Subject: Account readiness: prioritized health flags & exec hotlist

Team —

Preparing for Carpenter Inc.'s upcoming QBR (scheduled tentative 10/15). I pulled the health and renewal signals this morning; prioritizing the items that need executive attention so we can go into the QBR with a clear mitigation plan. Summary below (high level):

- Health: usage steady but 3 sustained spikes in token consumption have pushed projected spend 18% above committed baseline for the quarter.
- Performance: two incidents in Sept (short-lived) with P95 latency blips that impacted a subset of inference pipelines; engineering has a patch in staging.
- Support/Sentiment: CS notes increased ask volume around model-tail latency and custom prompt routing. Customer is asking for a stability SLO and clarified data retention policy.
- Commercial: renewal (annual) targeted for 11/30; procurement team flagged a required legal SLT clause and a potential discount ask if utilization continues.

Immediate asks:
1) Exec attention: confirm willingness to approve a one-time credit if actual usage > committed by >15% (we need a decision by 10/08).
2) Product/Infra: expedite the staging rollout for the hotfix and share expected rollback windows.
3) Sales/Legal: confirm procurement timeline and who will own contract redlines.
4) CS: prepare a one-pager on customer sentiment + top 3 asks (for the QBR slide deck).

Attachments: I exported the consumption extract and put a draft mutual action plan in the drive.

Irene — thanks for the concise breakdown. A couple quick notes inline and a proposed mitigation: 

> - Health: usage steady but 3 sustained spikes in token consumption have pushed projected spend 18% above committed baseline for the quarter.

We should confirm whether those spikes map to batch jobs or interactive traffic (I suspect the former after checking logs). If batch, a short-term throttling policy plus a one-time overage credit is the least disruptive path.

> - Performance: two incidents in Sept (short-lived) with P95 latency blips that impacted a subset of inference pipelines; engineering has a patch in staging.

Agreed we should prioritize the patch. Can infra provide an ETA for production rollout? If rollout will take >72 hours, I recommend we insert a temporary traffic split to a lower-cost model variant to avoid repeat incidents during the QBR window.

On credits: I support a limited, conditional credit up to 10% of monthly committed spend for Oct if the spikes are one-off and we implement protective throttles. Anything >15% should trigger an exec review.

Marcus
Head of Customer Ops
Redwood Inference
